findings.title: Small-action button float is ignored in the new flex row
findings.body: .small-action is now a flex container (the new flexbox() mixin sets display:flex), but its action button is still float:right. Float and clear do not apply to flex items, so the button is laid out in source order immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge. Short rows such as closed, pinned, or autoclosed actions therefore show the delete/expand control beside the text rather than pinned to the far side, in every browser that honors the new display. The same change also drops the description's 4em left padding that previously cleared the floated avatar, so non-flex fallbacks will overlap the icon and the text. Put margin-left:auto on the button (and drop the float) to restore the right alignment; .topic-avatar's float:left is likewise ignored and should not be relied on.

findings.title: Panel right-align does not work in the prefixed flex fallback
findings.body: .panel used to be float:right (and .title float:left). Those floats were removed and replaced with margin-left:auto plus order, while flexbox() emits display:-webkit-box and display:-moz-box before the modern values. The 2009 box model does not treat auto margins as flexible space, so browsers that only understand those prefixed values (Safari 6.1/7, iOS 7, older Android) keep the notifications, search, and login cluster immediately after the logo instead of on the right edge of the header. The prefixes this PR adds are exactly the browsers that will miss the new alignment, and there is no float fallback left.

findings.title: order() mixin writes a 0-based value into 1-based ordinal-group
findings.body: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based (initial value 1) and reject 0, while the modern order property and -ms-flex-order are 0-based (initial value 0). The new mixin assigns $val to all of them. Autoprefixer-style output must use $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group properties. order(2) and order(3) in this PR still sort after default items by accident (old default 1 is less than 2 and 3; modern default 0 is less than 2 and 3), but order(1) will not move an item after default siblings in old WebKit/Firefox, and order(0) or a negative order is invalid or ignored in the 2009 syntax. This is the shared helper the header now depends on, so the off-by-one should be fixed before it is reused.

findings.title: Header category bullet loses its 5px alignment offset
findings.body: .extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet previously had margin-top:5px so the category bullet lined up with the docked topic title text. That rule was deleted. The badges change only routes the existing display:inline-flex and align-items:baseline through mixins, so it does not add a replacement offset, and the new line-height:1.5 on the wrapper does not shift the bullet relative to the label. Category bullets in the scrolling header extra-info will sit about 5px too high against the category name.
